name: SayCan
one_liner: Multiplies LLM semantic task-step probabilities by RL value-function affordance scores to select physically feasible robot action plans.

loop.proposes: A language model scores candidate atomic robot skills by their semantic probability of advancing a high-level user instruction.
loop.judged_by: Pre-trained reinforcement-learning value functions (affordance critics) evaluate the exact probability that each skill will succeed from the current camera state.
loop.steers: Each step takes the highest-scoring skill by the joint product P(say) x V(can) until the termination token is reached; there is no beam or tree search.

headline_result: Executed 101 real-world mobile manipulation tasks in an office kitchen with 84% planning rate and 74% physical execution success.
caveat: Bounded by the repertoire of pre-trained low-level manipulation skills and cannot recover if an early step irreversibly alters the scene without replanning.
beyond_harness_note: Bellman value-function affordance critics gate every proposed language-model step according to physical execution feasibility.
algorithmic_authority: RL Bellman value-function affordance critics and physical robot controller

sources.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances (CoRL 2022 / arXiv:2204.01691)

verification.notes: Checked against Ahn et al., CoRL 2022.
